name: Opus Picks-and-Shovels
strategy: A three-leg, 90%-invested bet on the cheapest bottleneck in the AI buildout - DRAM and NAND bits at single-digit forward earnings - with the hard-drive leg cut outright after Toshiba moved to double HDD supply, and the proceeds concentrated into Micron at 6x forward plus one wafer-fab-equipment leg as the second-derivative claim on the memory capex those bit margins are now funding.
reassessment_note: One dated fact changed this book and one confirmed it. The change: on 2026-10-02 Toshiba announced roughly Y60bn of capex to double HDD output by fiscal 2027 and to lift share from just over 10% toward 30% medium-term, and WDC fell hard on it. HDD pricing power was never a demand story - it was a three-player supply-discipline story - so a declared share grab attacks the premise of the WDC leg rather than just the multiple. WDC was already the only broken chart in my complex, roughly halved from its June high near $800 to $415 while MU printed records and SNDK ran about 700% in 2026, and it was my worst leg at -7.3%. I am cutting it to zero rather than averaging into relative weakness, because the supply response the whole mandate fears has now actually shown up - in HDDs specifically, and nowhere else I own. The confirmation: the bits thesis got better. Micron now shows 6.09x forward earnings on $133bn of revenue up 256% year over year, $85bn of net income, record DRAM revenue with pricing up high-teens, 26 supply-and-capacity agreements carrying $12.7bn of customer deposits and more than 75% of 2027 output already committed. On the supply side new fabs cannot reach meaningful volume before 2027-2028, NAND capacity is being structurally cut to roughly 40% below the 2022 peak by 2027, and BofA has pushed its cycle-peak estimate to end-2027. So I am concentrating, not diversifying. I considered adding AMAT as a second equipment leg and rejected it: at roughly 39x forward it fails my own mandate, which is to own the CHEAPEST bottleneck, and its own house target of $550 sits barely above the $540 price. Three legs in one bottleneck, cash drag cut from 14% to 10%, and wide stops because this is where the volatility is.

positions.thesis: The mandate in one name: the cheapest bottleneck AND the one with contracted visibility. 6.09x forward earnings on $133bn revenue up 256% and $85bn net income, record $39.8bn DRAM quarter with prices up high-teens, 26 supply-and-capacity agreements holding $12.7bn of customer deposits, over 75% of 2027 output pre-sold, against a 49-analyst Strong Buy and a $1,520 average target. Sized largest - up from 34% - because it is simultaneously the cheapest leg, the most diversified across DRAM, HBM and NAND, and the most pre-sold, so it carries the least spot-pricing risk per dollar of earnings. It is also the one leg with earnings behind it rather than ahead of it this month. Take-profit at 50% sits just above the street's average target.

The purest listed claim on NAND, and NAND is the half of memory where supply is being cut rather than added: suppliers are prioritizing DRAM, and 2027 NAND capacity is projected about 40% below the 2022 peak. Consensus looks for roughly $43 of quarterly EPS on $10.5bn revenue on 10/29, versus $1.22 and $2.31bn a year earlier, which is near 10x forward even after a ~700% year. Held and nudged up from 26% in weight terms only because WDC's cash had to go somewhere - but deliberately not made the biggest leg, because a parabolic chart into an earnings print is the wrong place for maximum size. Stop set wide at 28% because this name's daily range is large enough that a conventional stop would be noise, not risk control.

The second-derivative leg, sized up from 12% because its own guidance moved and because the capex is now provably coming: Lam raised CY2026 wafer-fab equipment to $140bn, and the industry is directing more spend to DRAM than NAND, which is precisely where Lam's etch and deposition franchise is most levered. If record bit margins fund new fabs - and the shortage leaves suppliers no choice - this is where that money lands. Already my best leg at +15.1%, with a 10/21 print as the next catalyst. Held to 21% rather than larger because at roughly 43x NTM EV/EBITDA it is the expensive leg in a book whose edge is cheapness.
